subtopic: Schedule II and III quantity limits
stem: A prescriber orders a 90-day supply of phendimetrazine and authorizes refills. Which legal limits govern the pharmacy? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Schedule III status permits unlimited refills.
A non-opioid Schedule III prescription may qualify for a single fill of up to 90 days.
Authorized refills remain subject to federal count and time limits.
The weight-loss indication does not change the drug's Schedule III status.
Massachusetts treats the product as Schedule VI.

explanation.core_reasoning: The supported conclusions on these facts are: A non-opioid Schedule III prescription may qualify for a single fill of up to 90 days. Authorized refills remain subject to federal count and time limits. The weight-loss indication does not change the drug's Schedule III status.

choice_analysis.A: Not supported: Schedule III status permits unlimited refills.
choice_analysis.B: Supported: A non-opioid Schedule III prescription may qualify for a single fill of up to 90 days.
choice_analysis.C: Supported: Authorized refills remain subject to federal count and time limits.
choice_analysis.D: Supported: The weight-loss indication does not change the drug's Schedule III status.
choice_analysis.E: Not supported: Massachusetts treats the product as Schedule VI.

related_facts: phendimetrazine (Bontril) is used for short-term adjunct in a weight-reduction regimen; it is federal Schedule III and Massachusetts Schedule III.

Massachusetts generally limits Schedule II and III opioid prescriptions to a 30-day supply and recognizes defined 90-day pathways for OUD drugs, non-opioid Schedule II or III drugs, and implantable infusion pumps.
A Schedule III or IV prescription may not be filled or refilled more than six months after issue and may not be refilled more than five times unless renewed by the practitioner.
explanation.mpje_trap: Distinguish this near-miss from the controlling rule: 'Schedule III status permits unlimited refills.'

reasoning_steps: Classify phendimetrazine under the federal and Massachusetts schedules before selecting a legal pathway
